source_snapshot.message:
fix(mcp): close the in-process state leaks and the Windows install path

Review of #397 surfaced fifteen distinct defects in the new `ix mcp` layer.
They fall into three groups.

**The in-process runner leaks state that the process used to reset.**
A timed-out command is never cancelled, so it keeps writing to the process
globals after the queue advances: its late `process.exitCode = 1` was read by
whichever tool call was running by then, reporting a *successful* call as
failed with its real answer buried in an `error` string. `process.exitCode` is
a non-configurable accessor and cannot be made context-local, so instead a run
started while an abandoned command is still in flight ignores it and judges
only by what the command threw. `ix map`'s single-flight lock and
`resolve.ts`'s per-cwd scope cache had the same shape of bug — the process
ending *was* their invalidation — so the runner now releases held locks and
resets the scope cache after a command that can change either. And the
server no longer inherits main.ts's error handlers, whose every path ends in
`process.exit(1)`: a stray rejection from one tool call took down the whole
session and all 22 tools.

**Nothing registered on Windows, and every report said it had.**
`where ix` lists npm's extensionless `#!/bin/sh` shim first, which
CreateProcess cannot launch, and that is what was recorded into all seven
hosts. Host CLIs could not be spawned either — npm ships them as `.cmd`, which
Node refuses to spawn without a shell since CVE-2024-27980 — and the resulting
ENOENT was classified as a conflict, so install left every host alone.
Launcher resolution now takes the first PATHEXT-executable entry, and host
CLIs go through cmd as one pre-quoted string. A JSON argument cannot be
encoded that way at all (verified against a round-trip echo: cmd's quote
tracking flips mid-argument), so VS Code and openclaw write their documented
config shapes directly instead. A registration of ours whose launcher path has
since disappeared now reads as `stale` and is repaired without `--force`,
rather than reported healthy and skipped forever.

**Several paths answered confidently when they could not answer.**
`openclaw mcp show` failing was read as "nothing registered" and overwrote the
user's own server; `--host` with an unrecognised id filtered every host out and
exited 0; a JSONC config passed `inspect` and then hard-failed the write;
Cursor/VS Code/opencode were gated on shell shims they never invoke;
`ix_smells --path` matched by prefix where the rest of the CLI matches by
substring; `ix_inventory` required a path the CLI treats as optional and
dropped `--limit`; and every positional was passed bare, so `ix_text "--path"`
silently searched for something else.

Each fix carries a regression test, and each test was validated by restoring
the defect and confirming that test — not merely the suite — goes red.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
